posts.title: They Met With Us. Then Made It Worse.
posts.excerpt: We met with Council Members Pete Festersen and Danny Begley. They said they would try to include affordable housing, food access, and business relocation support in the TIF agreement. None of it appeared. Instead, they added a provision preventing renters from contesting property tax increases.
posts.author: Saddle Creek Merchants United + Grammercy Park Collective
posts.body:
## What They Said

Representatives from our coalition met with Council Members Pete Festersen and Danny Begley ahead of the Saddle Creek Marketplace TIF and EEA votes. We raised specific concerns and received specific responses. They told us they would try to include:

- Affordable housing units in the development
- A food access requirement, given Family Fare's departure from a neighborhood already facing food access challenges
- Support for the businesses being displaced, including relocation assistance

We left that meeting cautiously hopeful. We should not have been.

## What They Did

None of those commitments appeared in the final TIF agreement.

Instead, council added a provision that renters in the affected area cannot contest property tax increases. In a neighborhood where renters are already under pressure, this is not a neutral technical detail. It is a protection stripped from the people most vulnerable to displacement, written into a public subsidy agreement for a luxury apartment developer.

They did not try. They made it worse.

## What We Are Asking

We are asking every council member to vote NO on June 2. We are asking the mayor's office to intervene. And we are asking our neighbors, our community, and anyone who cares about how public money is spent in Omaha to show up or email before the final hearing.

Saddle Creek runs deep. We will not pay for our own displacement.

[Take action now.](take-action.html)

posts.title: WOWT: Neighbors Question $9M in Public Funding for Luxury Apartments
posts.excerpt: WOWT investigates the $110 million Saddle Creek Marketplace proposal: 223 luxury apartments, $9 million in TIF funding, no affordable housing, and a grocery gap that would leave the nearest store two miles away with no bus service.
posts.author: WOWT 6 News
posts.body:
## Coverage from WOWT 6 News

WOWT's First Alert 6 Investigations team reported on the Saddle Creek Marketplace proposal in January 2026, raising questions neighbors have been asking since the project was announced.

The development would replace the Midtown Plaza shopping center at 46th and Cuming with 223 luxury apartments and 67,000 square feet of retail space. The developer, Mitch Hohlen, is seeking $9 million in Tax Increment Financing from the city. The total project cost is $110 million.

Hohlen previously built The Artisan at 39th, also TIF-funded. Studios there start at $1,150 per month. Two-bedrooms run up to $2,470. The Saddle Creek Marketplace is described as similar.

### No affordable housing

Neighbor Josh Livingston told WOWT: "At that first meeting there were conversations about whether the units were going to be affordable and their indication was that was not part of their plan."

### The grocery gap

Family Fare's departure from Midtown Plaza would leave the nearest grocery store two miles away, with no direct bus service. Residents told WOWT they want assurance that food access will be addressed before any public money is committed.

### The TIF question

As Livingston put it: "TIF is obviously controversial. On the one hand, it's good for bringing redevelopment to the neighborhood. On the other hand you worry about who is making the most money off the TIF development."

**Read the full story:** [WOWT — Neighbors question $9M in public funding for luxury apartments](https://www.wowt.com/2026/01/29/neighbors-question-9m-public-funding-luxury-apartments-dundee-redevelopment/)

posts.title: Coalition Statement: End the N. Saddle Creek BID
posts.excerpt: Saddle Creek Merchants United and the Grammercy Park Collective are calling for the dissolution of the N. Saddle Creek Business Improvement District. Here is why, and what we want instead.
posts.author: Saddle Creek Merchants United + Grammercy Park Collective
posts.body:
## Our Position

Saddle Creek Merchants United and the Grammercy Park Collective are calling for the dissolution of the N. Saddle Creek Business Improvement District.

This is not a decision we came to lightly. A well-governed business improvement district can be a genuinely useful community institution. The N. Saddle Creek BID is not that. It has never been that.

## What the BID Actually Is

The BID's leadership consists of a developer and his wife, who live outside the neighborhood, a tenant of that developer, and one other absentee property owner. There is no meaningful local representation. The businesses required by law to fund it have no real voice in how it operates.

The BID meets at a storage facility two miles from Saddle Creek. It has never provided a transparent public accounting of how assessment funds are spent or how contractors are selected. It has required the BID to pay for private security to manage problems created by the developer's own neglected properties. It has been used to advance the interests of one or two individuals, not the neighborhood.

## The Road Closure

A public access road was closed at the developer's request, over the objections of businesses and residents who depend on it. The developer is now attempting to replat and sell that lot. A public road, closed for private gain, and now being converted into a private asset.

## What We Are Asking For

- Dissolution of the N. Saddle Creek BID in its current form
- A full independent audit of BID expenditures
- Reversal of the public road closure
- A moratorium on BID-related city council ordinances until a genuine community process has been completed
- Any future business improvement district for this corridor to be built from the ground up with authentic community governance

Contact us at saddlecreekbid@gmail.com.

posts.title: Welcome to the Saddle Creek Coalition
posts.excerpt: Saddle Creek Merchants United and the Grammercy Park Collective are joining forces. Here is who we are and what we are fighting for.
posts.author: Saddle Creek Merchants United + Grammercy Park Collective
posts.body:
## Two Organizations, One Goal

Saddle Creek Merchants United represents the independent businesses of the N. Saddle Creek corridor. Many of us are family-owned, deeply rooted in this neighborhood, and required by law to fund a Business Improvement District that has never represented our interests.

The Grammercy Park Collective was formed in 2022 by residents who found themselves shut out of the existing processes for giving feedback on development proposals affecting their neighborhood. When the association that was supposed to represent the neighborhood sided with developers, residents organized themselves.

We are joining forces because the problems facing Saddle Creek do not stop at the door of any single building or business. They affect everyone who lives and works here.

## What We Are Up Against

Two separate development projects closing in from both ends of the corridor. An unaccountable Business Improvement District controlled by outside developer interests. A $110 million luxury apartment proposal that would demolish seven businesses and a refugee services provider using $9 million in public TIF and EEA funding, with no affordable housing and no plan to replace the grocery access being lost.

Saddle Creek runs deep. We will not pay for our own displacement.

Email us at saddlecreekbid@gmail.com to get involved.
